Caharian, who shared the importance of understanding how AI can be used meaningfully rather than simply adopting the technology for its own sake. “The real opportunity for MSMEs is not simply to adopt AI para masabi na AI-enabled sila, but to really understand where it can create meaningful business value in terms of improving productivity, reducing operational costs, creating better customer experiences, or even possibly discovering entirely new business models," Caharian said. For GMA, that approach is particularly relevant as audiences increasingly consume content and interact with the network across digital platforms. GMA NMI serves as the network's innovation and technology center, helping drive its digital transformation through emerging technologies, new platforms, and technology-driven experiences for audiences. Its work also includes developing digital solutions, web applications, and interactive experiences designed to enhance engagement across multiple platforms. The company's involvement in the DTI initiative highlights the growing role of technology in the media industry, where networks are no longer limited to delivering programs through television but are also finding new ways to engage viewers online and across digital platforms. The AI & Scale-Up Center, a partnership between the DTI and Converge ICT Solutions, Inc., is intended to help businesses explore and integrate AI and other digital tools into their operations. For GMA, the push toward emerging technology forms part of its continuing evolution as a multi-platform content provider, with GMA NMI at the forefront of developing digital experiences for the network and its audiences.

One ducked under the addict’s net: A review of 'People, Places and Things'. Written by Duncan MacMillan, whose "Lungs" and "Every Brilliant Thing" have previously been mounted by The Sandbox Collective, the staged reading of "People, Places and Things" takes place over two days, Saturday, August 15, and Sunday, August 16, at the Black Box of the Proscenium Theater. Performances on both days are at 3 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. The opening scene takes us right into the self-destructing life of stage actress Emma. What follows is her attempt at rehabilitation in a clinic where other addicts of substance abuse are similarly facing their demons. The title comes from one of the steps to recovery, which has to do with facing head-on the "people, places and things" that trigger your addiction and the need to turn to these substances, whether alcohol or hard drugs. So yes, it is a staged reading, and one knows that I've always been a believer in having plays be staged and performed as they were meant to be. But as directed by Sab Jose-Gregorio, I have to admit this was the next best thing. It is a curious hybrid that goes beyond a mere reading, with cast members seated around a table. This production does employ a modicum of movement with book in hand, giving a strong picture of what it would have been like if properly staged. I, for one, would welcome that happening in the near future. My major reason would be the revelation that is film actress Bela Padilla as Emma. Bela alternates with Gabby Padilla in the lead role. While Gabby is a proven force in both theater and cinema, this is Bela's first spin on the stage. And what a powerhouse she turns out to be. Her constant motion, little tics, firm grasp of her lines, and capacity to play Emma as both stubborn and vulnerable, together with her command of her scenes in delivery and in occupying physical space, all point to a great future on stage, if she so chooses. Her stage presence was through the roof, and the audience watching the TDR (Technical Dress Rehearsal) with me obviously agreed. Jake Cuenca, Audie Gemora, Menchu Lauchengco-Yulo, Robbie Guevara, Reb Atadero, Brian Sy, Mariella Laurel, Pamela Imperial, Miel Abong, and Salve Van Schoonhoven complete the cast. As an ensemble, with books in hand, they still go through the motions and prove to be a very tight bunch, given the time they've had to rehearse this drama. Centered on addiction, deluding oneself, the factors that create the psychological crutch that these substances offer, and the difficult path to recovery, the drama tackles serious subject matter with shafts of dark humor. But yes, it is a "bleak house" kind of play, and the shadow of mental health looms continuously throughout the running time of close to three hours. Do make the effort to watch this, and you will be rewarded. And while I do praise Bela for her work here, I'm now actually curious to watch Gabby, as I've admired her work in the past. In other words, no matter who will be playing Emma when you watch, you'll be coming out a winner, having witnessed a great performance. Kudos to director Sab Jose-Gregorio, as I believe this is her directorial debut.

Japan's defense chief visits shrine neighbors see as symbol of Japanese militarism. TOKYO (AP) — The Japanese defense minister on Saturday prayed at Tokyo’s Yasukuni Shrine, seen by Japan’s Asian neighbors as a symbol of the country’s past militarism. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, despite repeated past pledges to visit on the day marking Japan's surrender, has so far stayed away from the shrine to avoid exacerbating diplomatic tensions. Visits by Japanese politicians to the shrine, which also commemorates World War II war criminals, have been criticized by China and South Korea. They see it as showing a lack of remorse over Japan’s wartime atrocities. Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi has regularly visited the controversial shrine to mark Japan's anniversary of the end of the war on Aug. 15 and other occasions. But as a defense minister pushing to increase Japan’s military capability and weapons sales under Takaichi’s hawkish government, his visit Saturday is seen as more contentious. The previous shrine visit by a defense minister was in 2024 by Minoru Kihara, the current chief secretary and top government spokesperson for Takaichi’s government. Japan’s Defense Ministry prohibits group visits by service members of the Self-Defense Forces, on grounds of constitutional separation of religion and state. Koizumi said in October it is natural for anyone in any country to pay respect for those who sacrificed their lives for their nation. Koizumi did not comment on the visit Saturday and walked past journalists at the shrine. He is the son of popular former Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi, who outraged China when he visited Yasukuni as a serving leader in 2006. Three executives from Takaichi’s governing Liberal Democratic Party also prayed together Saturday at the shrine and brought offerings in a rare joint visit on the prime minister's behalf that is seen as a move to make up for Takaichi’s absence and appeal to her right-wing supporters. Party secretary-general Shunichi Suzuki told reporters he prayed while keeping in mind the prime minister's thoughts for “the spirits of the war dead” and that he brought Takaichi’s cash offerings in her capacity as party leader. For Takaichi, appealing to right-wing voters is key at a time when her support is seen as rapidly falling, presumably over delayed economic measures addressing rising prices as well as scandals that include alleged negative election campaign videos and unpopular revisions to Japan's imperial family succession rules. Takaichi has not visited the shrine since taking office but has sent ornaments twice for the shrine’s biannual festivals. Tensions between Japan and China escalated in November when the Japanese leader said a Chinese attack on Taiwan could constitute “a survival-threatening situation” for Japan requiring the use of force. The comments enraged Beijing. Attention this week was on whether Takaichi, who has repeatedly said she would pray at the shrine on Aug. 15 despite the controversy, would keep her pledge and show up at Yasukuni on Saturday, when Japan marks its surrender that ended the war 81 years ago. Earlier this week, Kihara said Takaichi would make an appropriate decision, followed by Japanese media saying she would stay away from the shrine to keep Japan’s already difficult ties with Beijing from further worsening and maintain good ties with Seoul. The focus will shift later Saturday to how Takaichi describes the wartime history in her first address as prime minister at a national ceremony marking the surrender. Takaichi has repeatedly resisted acknowledging Japan's wartime aggression and atrocities, and denied that coercion was used against Korean laborers and women held as sex slaves for Japanese troops. She was previously part of a campaign to remove references to wartime sexual slavery, euphemistically known as “comfort women,” from school textbooks. She has said she is from the postwar generation who has no responsibility for Japan's past actions and that she has no intention to apologize. The country has faced revisionist pushbacks since the 2010s under nationalistic former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, who pushed to correct a “self-deprecating view” of Japan’s wartime history and regain national pride. Takaichi considers Abe a mentor. Since 2013, Japanese prime ministers have stopped apologizing to Asian victims for wartime atrocities, under a precedent set by Abe. Last year, however, former Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba expressed “remorse” over the war and called it a mistake, though he fell short of mentioning Japan's aggression across Asia or apologizing.

Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia's coast, toppling buildings and killing at least 5. MAUMERE, Indonesia (AP) — A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia early Saturday, collapsing buildings and homes, killing at least five people and causing panic in a region prone to deadly quakes. Authorities issued a tsunami warning and urged coastal residents to move to higher ground, but later lifted the warning when Indonesia’s Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency said monitoring showed no significant sea-level changes that would pose a threat to coastal communities. The U.S Geological Survey said the quake hit Indonesia's Flores region with a depth of 10 kilometers at 5:58 a.m. local time. Its epicenter was 68 km (42 miles) north-northwest of the city of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara province. The initial quake was followed by several aftershocks. East Nusa Tenggara police chief Rudi Darmoko said preliminary reports indicate two fatalities in Sikka Regency and three in Manggarai Regency as the earthquake caused severe damage and collapsed buildings. He said power outages in cities and villages have hampered the flow of information and complicated search and rescue efforts. “We are continuing to collect reports of damages and casualties, but there are communication disruptions,” Darmoko said, Footage on local television showed patients at several hospitals being evacuated from buildings as a precaution following the quake. Hospital staff moved equipment outdoors, including beds, IV stands and oxygen cylinders, and set up temporary treatment areas to adapt to emergency conditions. Quake felt on Flores island and other areas The quake was felt across much of Flores island with initial reports indicating heavy damage. Yohanna Embu, a resident of Sikka regency, said a number of buildings were damaged by the strong shaking and panicked people ran to higher ground. “Many buildings here were damaged ... I saw that the waiting room at the port terminal in Maumere had collapsed,” she said. Students at St. Peter Major Seminary in Sikka who were attending morning Mass fled in panic when the roof of an assembly hall collapsed, said the Rev. Guidelbertus Tanga, rector of the seminary, which is known locally as Ritapiret Seminary on the predominantly Catholic island of Flores. “Our students and nuns ran out in panic beneath a collapsing roof,” Tanga said. “At least one priest suffered a broken leg after jumping from the second floor of a building during the quake.” The quake also reportedly caused panic in Bima, a city in neighboring West Nusa Tenggara province. There were also damages reported in some part of southern Sulawesi island. Indonesian authorities initially issued a tsunami warning for parts of East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi provinces, and urged residents to stay away from beaches and riverbanks. The agency located the shallow undersea quake near Flores island. Indonesia prone to earthquakes Indonesia, a vast archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, is prone to earthquakes and volcanic activity because of its location on the “Ring of Fire,” an arc of volcanoes and fault lines in the Pacific Basin. A powerful earthquake caused a tsunami in 1992 that killed about 2,500 people on Flores, part of a group of islands in the eastern half of Indonesia. In 2018, a magnitude 7.5 quake spawned a large localized tsunami that wiped out coastal areas, while liquefaction caused by the shaking turned entire neighborhoods into rivers of sludge in the eastern Indonesian city of Palu, on the Palu-Koro Fault. The disaster killed more than 4,400 people. In 2010, a 10-foot (three-meter) wave struck the Mentawai Islands, off the western coast of Sumatra in Indonesia, just minutes after a massive offshore earthquake. More than 400 people were killed and hundreds of homes were destroyed. In December 2004, a massive magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra in western Indonesia triggered a tsunami that killed 230,000 people in a dozen countries.

US civil rights agency denies issuing order halting all federal class discrimination complaints. NEW YORK (AP) — A civil rights agency accused of halting a sexual harassment case filed on behalf of female prison guards is now blaming an administrative judge for doing so in error. A labor union and two female prison guards sued the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, which enforces employment anti-discrimination laws, for indefinitely suspending proceedings in their case as part of a wider effort to halt all federal-sector class claims pending before the agency's administrative judges. The lawsuit cited an administrative judge’s order dated Dec. 10, 2025, stating that the sexual harassment case had been paused and that the “notification applies to all class cases in the federal sector.” But in a court document filed Thursday evening, EEOC Chief Operating Officer Sharon Rose said the judge in the case issued the notification “in error” and that it was an “isolated incident.” Rose also told the court that the EEOC has transferred the case to another administrative judge, who on Monday issued an order scheduling further proceedings. The court document also included a letter sent by Justice Department attorney James Harlow to the plaintiffs on Monday, offering the same explanation and asking them to drop their motion for a preliminary injunction. “In short, Defendants agree that processing of federal-sector class complaints should not be suspended,” Harlow wrote in the letter. Joseph Sellers, co-chair of Cohen Milstein Sellers & Toll’s civil rights and employment practice and one of the attorneys for the plaintiffs, said Friday that the evidence belies the government's claim that the suspension was an erroneous isolated incident. Sellers and other attorneys involved in the lawsuit say they are representing federal workers in at least five other class complaints that have been stalled for months, including cases against the FBI and the Department of Defense. In two of those cases, administrative judges also issued scheduling orders Monday, according to the letter sent by Harlow, the Justice Department attorney. Harlow asked the attorneys to send him the name and number of any other federal-sector class complaints that may have been suspended “so we can investigate.” Sellers said the fact that the EEOC judges only ordered the scheduling orders this week, after the lawsuit was filed, suggests that the suspension was not an error. “The timing speaks for itself. We have evidence of a number of cases that were stayed. It is not an isolated incident as the EEOC seems to claim," Sellers said. Sellers said the plaintiffs are willing to engage in discussion with the Justice Department to resolve the issue outside the court. The lawsuit against the EEOC was filed by the American Federation of Government Employees, the largest union representing federal workers, and two women who are correctional officers at Louisiana’s Federal Correctional Complex at Pollock. The women are part of a pending class complaint claiming that management at Pollock failed to stop inmates from subjecting female workers to sexual harassment. Under President Donald Trump, the EEOC has drastically overhauled its civil rights enforcement priorities, including prioritizing cases aimed at stamping out diversity and inclusion policies, dropping cases on behalf of transgender workers and abandoning longstanding tools for investigating systemic discrimination. The changes have prompted several lawsuits against EEOC Chair Andrea Lucas, who says she is pursuing an “even-handed” and “colorblind” vision of workplace civil rights. Rose, the EEOC chief operating officer, said in her court statement that neither the commission nor Lucas had issued “a written or verbal directive to EEOC administrative judges” to indefinitely suspend class cases. The EEOC referred questions Friday to the Justice Department, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Avid fan buys late Pilita Corrales' house in Parañaque City. An avid fan has bought the Parañaque City home of late OPM icon Pilita Corrales, which was put up for sale earlier this year for a "negotiable" price of P26 million. Pilita's daughter, actress-singer Jackie Lou Blanco, said she is "very happy" that the buyer is a huge fan of her mother, making the sale of the family home more meaningful for them. "You know what, she's also a Bisaya. She's such a big, big fan of my mom," Jackie Lou said in an interview after the launch of National Artist Ricky Lee's latest book, "Quiapo Ilalim: Pagsusulat ng Iba't Ibang Daan," at Shangri-La Plaza mall. The house, located in an exclusive subdivision named after Jackie Lou herself, was first listed in January this year and was described as being priced "below market value." The property sits on a 466-square-meter lot, with a floor area of 453.57 square meters. The two-storey home has four spacious bedrooms, four bathrooms, a home office, and a four-car garage. It also comes with driver's and maids' quarters, as well as a solar water heater. For Jackie Lou, selling the property made practical sense since she and her half-brother, Ramon Christopher, already have homes of their own. "Wala na rin naman kasing titira sa bahay ng mom ko kasi all of us have our own. Yung adopted brother ko lang na si VJ ang nag-stay doon and the house is too big just for one person," she explained. "Okay na rin. I'm happy na napunta ang house ng mom ko sa kapwa Visayan. She's such a big fan of mom. At least it will be well taken care of," she added. Asked whether the buyer specifically purchased the property because of her admiration for Pilita, Jackie Lou was careful not to make assumptions. "Maybe it's just a coincidence," she said. Several other people were also interested in buying the property, but Jackie Lou felt that the eventual sale to the Visayan buyer was meant to happen. "I think it's really meant for her," she said. She added that the buyer has yet to move into the house as renovations are still ongoing. Known as the "Asia's Queen of Songs," Pilita remains among beloved figure in Philippine entertainment. She is celebrated for her distinctive voice and renditions of classics such as "Kapantay Ay Langit," "Usahay," and "A Million Thanks to You," among other songs. Pilita died peacefully in her sleep on April 12, 2025, at the age of 87.

Lacson flags ‘questionable’ infra lump sums in proposed 2027 budget. Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson on Saturday raised concerns over what he described as “questionable” lump-sum appropriations for infrastructure projects included in the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027. Lacson said he would seek clarification from the government agencies involved. Lacson says he may formally bring up the matter during the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) briefing, which is tentatively scheduled for Aug. 27. “We spotted lump sum appropriations that we don't think should be lump sum. When we say lump sum appropriations, an aggregate amount is appropriated for a project, activity or program (PAP), or group of projects without detailing the breakdown of the cost of each PAP,” he said in English and Filipino during an interview on DZMM radio. “We will seek clarification on the details of these lump sum appropriations. Lump sum appropriations are allowed for calamity funds because we cannot predict when calamities occur. But it becomes questionable if it's for infrastructure projects. That is what we saw and we will ask for details on the matter,” he added. Lacson and his staff have begun reviewing the National Expenditure Program (NEP), which was transmitted to Congress earlier this week. Aside from the lump-sum allocations, Lacson said they would examine the NEP for special provisions that could potentially be used to circumvent restrictions on unprogrammed appropriations. He recalled a previous General Appropriations Act (GAA) in which the bicameral conference committee inserted two provisions he described as “highly questionable, even unconstitutional". One provision allowed the executive branch to transfer funds from government-owned and controlled corporations (GOCCs), including the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth), to the national treasury. Another involved Foreign Assisted Projects, which Lacson said could have allowed funds to be used for purposes other than those for which they were intended. Both provisions were later removed from succeeding national budgets. Lacson also said he intends to preserve budget reforms introduced by the Senate and carried through the bicameral conference committee under then-Senate finance committee chairman and now Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian. These include livestreaming bicameral proceedings and making budget-related documents publicly available online. He said current finance committee chairman Sen. Jose Victor “JV” Ejercito had assured him that he would not permit insertions during the bicameral conference committee if they were not included in either the Senate or House versions of the General Appropriations Bill. “I hope this year that under Sen. JV's chairmanship, he will fulfill his promise not to allow insertions at the bicam level,” Lacson said. Lacson said enforcing the policy would help address the long-standing practice of adding provisions during the final stages of the budget process that were absent from both the Senate and House versions of the spending bill. He also renewed his call for local government units and local development councils to have a larger role in determining budget priorities. He said the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) should adjust the timing of its budget call so that proposals from local development councils, coursed through Regional Development Councils, can be considered for inclusion in the NEP. According to Lacson, greater participation by local officials could help bridge the gap between the needs of communities and projects inserted by lawmakers without consulting the officials concerned. He recalled a case involving a fishing community in Bicol, where fishermen had asked for his assistance because they had to use an improvised “skateboard” or flatbed trolley along railroad tracks before taking a tricycle and jeepney to transport their catch to market. The lack of a bridge meant the journey took nearly an entire day. After funding was secured for the bridge, travel time was cut by around 45 minutes. Lacson also pointed to President Marcos' Executive Order (EO) No.82, issued in January 2025, which sought to strengthen the participation of regional development councils in the budget process. Despite the order, however, Lacson said local officials continue to go to the Senate to seek funding for projects that were not included in the NEP. “I was hoping EO 82 would be implemented properly but it seems the situation has not quite been corrected. This early we see many mayors visiting the Senate, telling us that their projects did not make it to the NEP. There is a disconnect. This is what I have been advocating since I entered the Senate 20-plus years ago. Local development councils must be given attention because they know their constituents' needs,” he said.

3 reasons to buy bank-repossessed vehicles. If you are looking for your first vehicle, or perhaps a vehicle to use for your business, you might want to consider visiting your bank. Banks, like CBS, are often overlooked as an option when it comes to car purchases. But at each bank, there are great deals to be had. All you need to do is ask. Banks routinely sell repossessed cars, SUVs, pickups, and vans through bidding and negotiated sales, often at prices significantly below comparable market listings. Acquired Assets Division Head Jun L. de Guzman says partnering with a bank is the most logical thing to do when it comes to making large purchases. “You already look to banks to buy brand new cars or real estate. Partnering with banks to buy repossessed vehicles is just as intuitive. You are assured the transaction will be above board as banks go the extra mile to ensure documentation is done correctly.” Here are a few more reasons to buy bank-repossessed vehicles 1. You can buy below market value The biggest advantage of repo vehicles is the price. Banks are not car dealers. Their goal is to recover outstanding loan balances and dispose of non-performing assets as quickly as possible. As a result, many repossessed vehicles are offered at substantial discounts compared to equivalent used-car listings. Numerous bank auctions feature relatively recent-model vehicles with bid prices well below their original purchase prices. 2. Many units are surprisingly new A common misconception is that all repossessed vehicles are old or heavily used. In reality, bank inventories frequently include cars that are only one to three years old, with relatively low mileage. Listings can even include 2026 model-year vehicles. 3. Banks offer transparent buying processes Most banks sell vehicles through public bidding, online auctions, or negotiated sales with documented procedures and complete ownership records. Buyers can typically inspect units before bidding and review vehicle details, mileage, and condition disclosures. For budget-conscious buyers, bank-repossessed vehicles can be one of the smartest ways to acquire a car. But be wary, this isn’t exactly a secret, and competition for those vehicles can be steep. Many secondhand vehicle dealers go to banks and buy in bulk regularly. If you want those steep discounts, you will have to be ready to outbid other parties. You will need to check if the vehicle you want is available. Banks do not hold on to repossessed vehicles for very long. Learn more about CBS China Bank Savings’ repossessed vehicle inventory and its bidding process at www.cbs.com.ph.

Marvel drops 'VisionQuest' trailer at D23, bringing back Vision and Ultron. Marvel has dropped the first trailer for "VisionQuest," giving fans their first major look at Paul Bettany's return as Vision and James Spader's comeback as Ultron. The trailer debuted during the Disney Entertainment Showcase at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event on Friday at the Honda Center in Anaheim, where Bettany and Spader joined Marvel Studios president and executive producer Kevin Feige onstage. The trailer and poster were also released online for fans to watch. In "VisionQuest," Vision has been rebooted and is trying to find a new purpose after escaping those who wanted to weaponize him. Still struggling to understand his identity and existence, Vision turns to the AI personas embedded in his programming, including F.R.I.D.A.Y., E.D.I.T.H., J.A.R.V.I.S., and Ultron. His attempt at a quiet life comes to an end after a bounty is placed on him, forcing Vision to go on the run with Thomas Shepard, a mysterious boy who may be connected to him as his son. The trailer also gives fans a new look at Vision's complicated relationship with Ultron, the artificial intelligence who helped create him and later became one of the MCU's most dangerous villains. For fans of "WandaVision," the return of Vision is particularly significant. The character last appeared in the 2021 Disney+ series after being rebuilt by S.W.O.R.D. as the all-white Vision. "VisionQuest" picks up his story as he attempts to reconcile his new existence with the memories of the original Vision. Spader's return as Ultron is another major draw. The actor last played the character in 2015's "Avengers: Age of Ultron," where the artificial intelligence turned against humanity and was ultimately defeated by Vision. "VisionQuest" will serve as the final chapter of the television trilogy that began with "WandaVision" in 2021 and continued with "Agatha All Along" in 2024. Apart from Bettany and Spader, t he new series also stars Ruaridh Mollica, Todd Stashwick, T'Nia Miller, Lauren Morais, Orla Brady, Diane Morgan, Polly Frame, Henry Lewis, Jonathan Sayer, Emily Hampshire, and James D'Arcy. Christopher J. Byrne, Gandja Monteiro, Vincenzo Natali, and Terry Matalas direct the series. Matalas also serves as creator for television, with Cindy Appel, Christopher Monfette, Nicole Falsetti, and Matthew Okumura among the writers. "VisionQuest" premieres exclusively on Disney+ on October 14.

Prosecution makes case for public chat on trial before Escudero hands down crucial ruling. Filipinos would certainly be on the losing end should a gag order on public pronouncements about Vice President Sara Duterte's Senate impeachment trial get imposed. House prosecution members and spokespersons stated this in no uncertain terms even as they await presiding officer Senator-judge Francis "Chiz" Escudero's ruling on the matter this coming Monday, Aug. 17. While they would respect whatever decision the Senate impeachment court would have, solon-prosecutors Bicol Saro Party-list Rep. Terry Ridon and Manila 3rd district Rep. Joel Chua are still compelled to favor a non-restictive public discussion on the impeachment. Fake news explosion? The contrary could open the floodgates for fake news, they warned. “The further you restrict official communications by the defense, the prosecution, and the court itself, dyan po nagkakaroon ng (there could be a) vacuum for misinformation, disinformation, fake news,” Ridon said. He said the clear line should be against fake news, misinformation, and disinformation—not legitimate explanations of what actually transpired in open court. “It does not serve the interest of the public pagka po magkakaroon ng further restrictions on trying to explain to the public yung pong pagtakbo ng mga proceedings po na ito,” Ridon said. (It does not serve the interest of the public if there are further restrictions on trying to explain to the public how these proceedings are being conducted.) “Every piece of evidence, technical man ito, ay dapat na ipapaliwanag ng bawat partido, ng depensa, ng prosekusyon, kahit ng korte mismo sa ating pong taong-bayan,” he noted. (Every piece of evidence, whether technical or not, should be explained by each party—the defense, the prosecution, even the court itself—to our people.) While Chua acknowledged that the prosecution is bound by the Senate impeachment rules, he said some flexibility should be allowed so the public can better understand what is happening inside the impeachment court. “Ang impeachment kasi, this is imbued with public interest. Bakit po namin sinabing public interest? Unang-una, ito po nasasakdal o yung subject po ng impeachment ay public official na hinalal ng taong-bayan," Chua said. (Impeachment is imbued with public interest. Why do we say public interest? First of all, the subject of impeachment is a public official elected by the people.) “Kung hindi naman namin maipapaliwanag, lalong-lalo na po kami na nasa prosecution, kasi kami ang nakita ng kabuuan ng presentasyon ng ebidensya. Kung hindi naman namin ito maipapaliwanag nang maayos sa ating mga kababayan, ay baka hindi rin nila maunawaan kung ano po talaga ang nangyayari sa loob po ng impeachment court,” he said. (If we, especially those of us in the prosecution who have seen the entirety of the evidence presentation, cannot explain this properly to our fellow citizens, then they might not understand what is really happening inside the impeachment court.) Ridon says press briefings, media interviews, and social media posts by the prosecution are intended to help Filipinos understand the often technical proceedings and the evidence presented before the court. Currently, the House prosecution panel conducts near daily press conferences on the high-stakes trial against Duterte based on four articles of impeachment . Spliced videos are more dangerous Aside from the prosecutors themselves, spokesperson Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong and Robert Ace Barbers have been fixtures in these daily briefings. They agree that restricted discussions isn't the way to go. The two also expressed great concern over the spread of what they described as “spliced videos” on social media about the impeachment trial. Adiong said the so-called sub judice rule should not be enforced selectively against either the prosecution or defense. Barbers said these short edited video clips and selective excerpts of the hearings pose a greater danger to public understanding than responsible commentary from the parties in the trial. "When testimony is taken out of context, the public is left with only half the story. Selective content can easily distort the evidence and create false narratives that spread much faster than the truth," the ex-solon from Mindanao said. He stressed that impeachment proceedings should be evaluated based on the totality of the evidence presented before the Senate and not on isolated sound bites designed to generate online engagement or political advantage. "The impeachment trial is a constitutional process of immense national importance. It should be decided on facts and evidence presented before the Senate—not by viral posts, selective video clips, or online misinformation," he said. "The public deserves the truth in its full context, and every participant in the national conversation shares the responsibility of protecting it," Barbers added.

PCSO donates advanced ultrasound equipment; releases Lotto share to Bulacan. MALOLOS CITY, Bulacan – The Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) recently donated a 2D Echocardiography Ultrasound with Doppler to the Emilio G. Perez Memorial District Hospital and released more than ₱1.8 million in lotto shares to the provincial government of Bulacan during a ceremony held at the Bulacan Provincial Capitol. Leading the activity was PCSO General Manager Melquiades A. Robles, together with Directors Janet De Leon Mercado, Jennifer Liongson-Guevara, and Imelda Papin. During the ceremony on August 3,2026, Robles and Bulacan Governor Daniel Fernando signed a Deed of Donation formalizing the turnover of the advanced medical equipment, which is expected to strengthen the hospital’s diagnostic capabilities and improve patient care. Dr. Gerardo Morales, chief of hospital and medical director of Emilio G. Perez Memorial District Hospital, expressed his appreciation to the PCSO, saying the equipment will greatly benefit Bulakeño patients in need of quality healthcare services. The equipment donation was made under the PCSO’s Medical Equipment Donation Program (MEDP), which provides qualified hospitals with modern medical equipment to help improve healthcare services nationwide. In addition, PCSO turned over ₱1,808,156.64, representing Bulacan’s share from lotto revenues for the period covering January to June 2026. The release of lotto shares is in accordance with Executive Order No. 357-A, which allocates a portion of lotto revenues to local government units to support healthcare, social welfare, and other community-based programs.

PCSO donates medicines to barangays in Pangasinan and Manila. MANDALUYONG CITY — The Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) recently donated medicines worth ₱30,000 each to Barangay Poblacion in Malasiqui, Pangasinan, and Barangay 413 in Manila through its Medicine Donation Program during a ceremonial turnover held at the PCSO Conservatory Building in Mandaluyong City. Representing the PCSO management, Division Chief III Dr. Rouel Aparato led the turnover of the medicine packages, reaffirming the agency's commitment to making basic healthcare assistance more accessible to communities. Barangay Poblacion Chairperson Francisco Mejia Jr. and Barangay 413 Chairperson Rafael Mendoza Jr. personally received the donated medicines on behalf of their respective constituents during the ceremony held on Aug. 3, 2026,. The barangay officials thanked PCSO for the assistance, noting that the medicines will be distributed to indigent residents to help address their basic healthcare needs. The Medicine Donation Program is one of PCSO's initiatives aimed at providing essential medicines to local government units and communities, particularly those with limited access to healthcare services. The program complements the agency's charitable mandate by supporting grassroots health initiatives and improving access to basic medical assistance.

LPA unlikely to become storm, affect PH; habagat to bring rains —PAGASA. The low-pressure area (LPA) being monitored outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) is unlikely to develop into a tropical cyclone or affect any part of the country, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Saturday, Aug. 15. PAGASA weather specialist Veronica Torres said the LPA was last located 2,270 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon as of 3 a.m. “Mayroon tayong mino-monitor na low-pressure area sa labas ng ating Philippine Area of Responsibility (We are monitoring a low-pressure area outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility),” she said. “Itong LPA na ito ay napakababa ng tyansa na maging isang ganap na bagyo in the next 24 hours (This LPA has a very low chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within the next 24 hours).” Torres added that the weather disturbance is moving farther away from the Philippine landmass. “Itong low-pressure area na ito, mababa ‘yung tiyansang makaapekto sa kahit anong parte ng ating bansa. At ito nga ay papalayo na rin sa ating landmass (This low-pressure area has a low chance of affecting any part of the country. It is also moving farther away from our landmass),” she said. Meanwhile, PAGASA said the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” continues to affect Luzon and the western section of the Visayas. The weather specialist said the “habagat” will bring rains over a large portion of Luzon, including Metro Manila.

Radioactive hazards discovered in raided steel plant in Davao. The raid in a steel manufacturing site in Davao City has exposed the presence of nuclear or radioactive materials that are hazardous not only to the environment but also to the people exposed to them. Undersecretary Benjamin C. Acorda, Jr., head of the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC), said the presence of the radioactive isotopes was confirmed in the finished products at the Davao Mighty Steel (DMS) Corporation as attested by the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (PNRI) He said PNRI’s further investigation revealed that the hazardous radioactive isotopes were also present furnace-related materials, residual black sand, industrial powders, dust, wastes, wastewater, and other production and stored materials in the steel factory located in Barangay Ilang, Bunawan, Davao City where 174 Filipinos were working. The Filipino workers were rescued in the operation led by the National Bureau of Investigation on Thursday, Aug. 13. “Technical examinations confirmed the presence of radioactive isotopes, including Uranium-238, Thorium-228, Thorium-232, and Radium-226, across different stages and areas of the company's operations,” the PAOCC statement read. The raided steel manufacturing company has no permit to acquire, receive, possess, use, store, sell, transfer, import, or export nuclear or radioactive materials, according to the PNRI. The DENR inspection likewise found that the company's Environmental Compliance Certificate did not declare or authorize the presence, handling, processing, storage, or use of radioactive materials within the facility,” PAOCC added. The presence of radioactive materials was also monitored in the raided steel manufacturing companies in Misamis Oriental and in Pampanga. Substandard? Aside from radioactive materials concern, Acorda said separate product-standard testing also raised serious concerns over the company’s reinforcing steel already circulating in the market. Of eight samples purchased from commercial hardware establishments across Mindanao, he said four, or 50 percent, failed the mandatory mass-variation requirement. The substandard issue was also the major concern in the same two steel companies raided in Misamis Oriental and in Pampanga. Case build-up Acorda said the case was already referred by the NBI to the Department of Justice for appropriate proceedings. The referred cases include violations of Republic Act No. 12305 or the Philippine National Nuclear Energy Safety Act, Republic Act No. 6969 or the Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act; Presidential Decree No. 1586 or the Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System; and Republic Act No. 7394 or the Consumer Act of the Philippines.

Glaiza de Castro gets emotional remembering the late Ricky Davao at '58th' screening. Glaiza de Castro was visibly holding back tears as she talked about Ricky Davao after the special screening of “58th” at Cinemalaya Thursday night. The actress had just watched the film with us at Shangri-La Plaza in Mandaluyong City, and she was beaming as she shared how proud she was to be part of such a meaningful project. But when the questions turned to Davao, the night became personal for her. Davao plays her father in the film, but their relationship went beyond what viewers will see on screen. “Lagi kong naaalala sa kanya, he’s just so jolly sa set,” De Castro told us. She smiled as she recalled how they worked together on “58th” while also doing “Encantadia Chronicles: Sang'gre” and “Sinagtala.” At one point, she even teased him about taking on so much work. “Direk, ang sipag mo naman, parang lahat na ginawa mo,” she recalled telling Davao. Then there's the belt. Davao had given her one while they were shooting “58th,” showing her how to use it to secure her lapel microphone. It was something he had picked up from his theater experience. She eventually misplaced it. But when she finally found it again, it was also when she learned that Davao had passed away. Davao died on May 1, 2025 at 63 after battling cancer. De Castro also shared what Davao's daughter, Rikkie Mae, told her. She said De Castro was one of her father's favorite actors to work with. That was when the actress started getting emotional. “Naiiyak ako kasi special sa akin si Direk Ricky,” she said, noting how Davao had been her director in "Grazilda," her first titular lead role. “Naging director ko rin siya sa ‘Sang'gre,’” she said. “Hindi lang siya co-actor for me, siguro siya yung natuturing kong tatay sa showbiz.” It was ironic, considering that Davao's final screen role was that of her character's father. In “58th,” Davao plays Reynaldo “Bebot” Momay, a photojournalist who was among those killed in the 2009 Maguindanao massacre. His remains were never found. His daughter, Reynafe, played by De Castro, continues the fight to have him recognized as the 58th victim. The film has already been screened abroad, including at the International Film Festival Rotterdam and Doc Edge in New Zealand. But De Castro had been waiting for the film to finally be shown in the Philippines. “It’s different when it’s shown here in the Philippines. The impact is different,” she said. “58th” is not an easy story. The Nov. 23, 2009 massacre claimed 58 lives, including 32 journalists. But because Momay's remains were never recovered, only 57 victims were included in the court's murder convictions. That is where the film gets its title. De Castro knows some people may find the subject difficult to watch, but she believes that is also why it needs to be seen. “I know it’s not a light story, but it’s one of those stories that we shouldn’t forget,” she said. She is particularly proud that the film can introduce the tragedy to a new generation. “I’m proud to have been part of it and to be able to share with the new generation what happened.” “I know na telling this story served its purpose at bilang isang aktor, isa yun sa mga goals ko na makapagsabi rin kung ano yung totoo,” she added. That is what made the Cinemalaya screening different for De Castro. She was there to celebrate “58th” finally being shown to Filipino audiences, but she was also watching the final screen performance of someone she considered more than a co-star. Someone she called her “tatay sa showbiz.”

3 rallyists face arrest warrants in viral Labor Day cop assault. Three rallyists accused of assaulting a police officer during a Labor Day protest in Manila now face arrest warrants issued by a Manila court, the Manila Police District (MPD) said. On Saturday, August 15, MPD said the Metropolitan Trial Court in Manila has issued warrants against the three for alleged violation of Article 153 of the Revised Penal Code, or tumults and other disturbances of public order. The case stemmed from a May 1, 2026, incident along T.M. Kalaw Avenue in Ermita, where a police officer documenting the protest was allegedly assaulted during a confrontation with rallyists. Police had earlier reported that the officer was allegedly punched, scratched, and struck with a bamboo stick, while his cellphone was also reportedly taken during the incident. The incident happened during the May 1 Labor Day protests, when protesters had gathered at Welcome Rotonda and later moved toward Mendiola. Some groups proceeded to T.M. Kalaw Avenue and Roxas Boulevard after their advance was blocked. A video of the confrontation was later widely circulated on social media . Following the court's issuance of the warrants, MPD personnel were directed to locate and apprehend the three accused in accordance with existing laws and procedures. MPD District Director Brig. Gen. Arnold C. Santiago said the district would enforce the court's order while observing the rights of all parties involved. “The Manila Police District remains steadfast in upholding the rule of law, ensuring the lawful enforcement of court processes, and protecting the rights of all parties concerned,” Santiago said. The MPD did not identify the three rallyists in its statement.

Taiwan Day 2026 brings Taipei ticket raffle, human claw machine to One Ayala. The Taiwan Tourism Administration will host “Taiwan Day 2026”, the first flagship event of its 2026 promotional campaign in the Philippines, on August 22-23 at Level 2, Concourse, One Ayala in Makati City. Admission is free, and the event runs from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. on both days. According to the latest statistics from the Taiwan Tourism Administration, 400,827 Filipino visitors traveled to Taiwan in the first half of 2026, representing a 28% increase compared to 312,821 visitors during the same period in 2025. The Philippines has remained Taiwan’s largest source market in Southeast Asia. To keep arrivals climbing, the Taiwan Tourism Administration has built its 2026 Philippine campaign around the theme “Taiwan 100 Ways.” The campaign sets out four travel themes and pairs each with a Filipino creator who has more than 1 million followers. The event launches the “Taiwan 100 Ways - Film Your Way” short-video contest, inviting people across the Philippines to show new ways of traveling in Taiwan from their own perspectives. Top influencers explore Taiwan: Four themes revealed Social media plays a large part in how Filipinos plan trips, so the Taiwan Tourism Administration invited four leading creators to document a different side of Taiwan. On the food route, “Waves of Flavor”, fashion and lifestyle creator Laureen Uy-Cruz explores Michelin Guide restaurants, including Michelin-Starred and Bib Gourmand picks, in Taipei, Taichung, Tainan and Kaohsiung. On the culture route, “Waves of Culture”, the duo behind travel blog The Poor Traveler visits Tamsui Old Street, Tangweigou Hot Spring Park in Jiaoxi, Yilan County, and the Fulong International Sand Sculpture Art Festival, showcasing the charm of Taiwanese festivals and old-street culture. On the outdoor route, “Waves of Vitality”, vlogger-actor Kimpoy Feliciano heads to Sun Moon Lake, the Formosan Aboriginal Culture Village and Guguan Hot Springs, to experience various outdoor activities in Taiwan. On the stopover route, “Waves of Stopover”, former flight attendant Jen Barangan-David shows how passengers with a long layover at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport can visit the Danjiang Bridge, Tamsui Old Street, Dihua Street in Dadaocheng, the National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, Ximending and Taipei 101. Among the highlights is the newly completed Danjiang Bridge, designed by Zaha Hadid Architects and inspired by the movement of Cloud Gate Dance Theatre dancers. It has the world’s longest main span for a cable-stayed bridge carried on a single off-center tower. Visitors on the bridge look out over the Tamsui River estuary, from afternoon light to sunset to the lighted skyline at night, making it an ideal spot for taking photos and checking in. The bridge also improves regional connectivity while linking the North Coast’s scenic mountain and coastal attractions, with strong potential to attract international visitors. Interactive Stations and On-Site Highlights The venue features four immersive themed stations. Visitors collect stamps on a digital card as they go. Three stamps earn an entry into the raffle for round-trip tickets between Manila and Taipei, courtesy of EVA Airways. Four stamps earn a turn at the Human Claw Machine, where players have a chance to grab Taiwanese prizes. The event also includes the “Taiwan Connection Station”, a retro-style phone booth encouraging visitors to reach out to family and friends in Taiwan. Short-video Contest The “Taiwan 100 Ways - Film Your Way” contest is open to all Filipinos, whether or not they have been to Taiwan. Entries must be 30 to 60 seconds long and shot vertically for Instagram Reels or YouTube Shorts. They may use footage from an actual trip or build an original concept inspired by Taiwan. Submissions open Aug. 22, 2026, and close Jan. 15, 2027. Winners will be announced at “Taiwan Day 2027” in Cebu in March 2027. Full contest rules and entry details are posted on the official Facebook page: Taiwan Tourism PH (facebook.com/TaiwanTourismPH). Filipino fencers reap medals in SEA FF. Filipino fencers shone at the Southeast Asian Fencing Federation (SEAFF) Junior and Cadet Fencing Championship after collecting five gold, seven silver and 13 bronze medals in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia recently. Oscar del Castillo led the charge for the Filipinos with a gold medal in the 17-under cadet men’s epee, while Willa Galvez, Victoria Ebdane and Jodie Tan also bagged the junior women’s foil team gold. Also ruling their respective team events are Ebdane, Tan, Yuna Canlas and Hagia Del Castillo in the cadet women’s foil team; Khiane Felipe, Vito Coching, Drake Chung and Matthew General in the sabre junior men’s team; and Del Castillo, Joaquin de Silos, Jacob Mayo and Li Jiashu in the epee cadet men’s team. Going home with silver medals were Oscar Del Castillo (21-under junior men’s epee individual), Hagia Del Castillo (cadet women’s foil individual), the cadet women’s foil team of Galvez, Christine May Morales and Victoria Malvar; the women’s epee team of Papina Torre, Eleina Junia and Faith Olemos; the junior women’s saber team of Estelliah Gilliana, Hailey Peters, Arianna Tiu and Nadelle Turiano; the cadet men’s sabre team of Drake Chung, Marcus Co Say, Erlon Mallari and Sean Ragos; and the cadet women’s sabre team of Ryona Salvante, Elise Acuzar, Ruth Nierras and Estelliah Gillana pocketed a silver in cadet women’s sabre. Galvez, whose competition abroad is supported by Nickel Asia Corporation, with backing from Converge, NLEX Corporation, Rain or Shine, MVP Sports Foundation, Strong Group Athletics, Pocari Sweat and Icons Sports Management Services, also bagged the bronze in the junior women’s foil individual. Also bringing home the bronze were Ebdane and Canlas (women’s foil individual), Don Geronimo (cadet men’s epee), Jethro Chan (cadet men’s foil), Papina Torre (cadet women’s epee); the junior men’s team epee of Geronimo, Mayo, de Silos and del Castillo; the junior women’s foil team of Canlas, Del Castillo and Malvar; the junior women’s epee of Junia, Olemos, Torre and Rhiana Cruz; the junior men’s foil team of Inigo Divinagracia, Lucas Palafox, Elijah Timbol and Chan; the cade women’s epee team of Cruz, Summer Feliciano and Chiara Guidote; the cadet men’s sabre team of Luis Clemente, Ynigo Estrada and Qody Omengan; and the cadet men’s foil team of Chan, Palafox and Yohann Roldan.

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. ORIGI, MESSIAS, ADLI E 25 MILIONI PER MILINKOVIC-SAVIC. LOTITO NE CHIEDE 35!!!. Il Milan, dopo lo scioccante siluramento di Paolo Maldini, punta al grande colpo per il calciomercato estivo: Sergej Milinkovic-Savic della Lazio . Lo ha riferito ' SportMediaset '. Il Diavolo, dunque, ha intenzione di andare all'assalto del centrocampista serbo, classe 1995 , che gioca nella Capitale dal 2015 e che ora sembra arrivato al momento dei saluti. Nonostante il contratto di Milinkovic-Savic scadrà tra un anno, il 30 giugno 2024 , il Presidente della Lazio, Claudio Lotito , continua a valutarlo molto. Si parla di 35-40 milioni di euro, per un giocatore che, in fin dei conti, in questa stagione con le Aquile di Maurizio Sarri si è riconfermato come uno dei centrocampisti più forti e completi del panorama calcistico mondiale. Motivo per cui il Milan, pur di metterlo a disposizione di Stefano Pioli in questo calciomercato estivo, sarebbe pronto ad offrire alla Lazio 25 milioni più ben tre contropartite tecniche individuati in Junior Messias , Divock Origi e Yacine Adli. Le contropartite tecniche sarebbero di gradimento per Mister Sarri e si adatterebbero facilmente al suo gioco spettacolare: Adli può ricoprire diversi ruoli del centrocampo e sarebbe un sostituto ideale del capitano biancoazzurro; Messias , visto il flop di Romero e l'età avanzata di Pedro, sarebbe un'ottima alternativa di fascia visto i tanti impegni che aspettano la Lazio; Origi sarebbe una discreta opzione a Ciro Immobile, lasciando crescere con tranquillità il talentuoso Cancellieri. La palla passa a Lotito che attende un rialzo di offerta magari intorno ai 30 milioni e l'inserimento di tre contropartite tecniche di buon livello per concludere l'affare.

Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

BONUS VACANZE: SCADENZA DELLE DOMANDE IL 30 GIUGNO. La procedura per la richiesta del Bonus vacanze va effettuata solamente online tramite la app “Io” da smartphone. Basta munirsi di Spid o della carta d’identità elettronica. Lo possono richiedere soltanto i nuclei familiari con un reddito Isee sotto i 40.000 euro e può essere speso solo per un soggiorno in Italia entro la fine dell’anno. Una volta ottenuto il Bonus, la prenotazione della vacanza non può essere effettuata su siti online: quindi non è possibile prenotare né con Booking né con Airbnb o con altri siti di prenotazione. Bisogna, invece, prenotare tramite agenzie viaggi o o tour operator tradizionali o direttamente con la struttura scelta nella meta di villeggiatura. Ecco gli step per fare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze: se non si è già scaricata la app “Io” in passato sul proprio smartphone è possibile farlo sia per telefoni Apple sia per Android; la prima volta che si scarica la app viene richiesta la registrazione che è possibile fare più facilmente digitando un Pin a scelta o, per chi è più pratico, attraverso il riconoscimento biometrico (impronta digitale o riconoscimento del volto); una volta entrati nella app, bisogna selezionare la sezione “pagamenti” e quindi il Bonus vacanze; a questo punto è necessario inserire le informazioni richieste, tra cui il valore dell’Isee; se tutte le informazioni inserite sono corrette, la app genera un codice associato al vostro Bonus vacanze con un QrCode; sia il codice sia il QrCode devono essere mostrati alla struttura al momento del pagamento. N.B. Prima di effettuare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze è bene tenere sotto mano sia la propria identità Spid sia la carta d’identità elettronica e i dati del proprio Isee (chi non lo ricorda può recuperarlo all’Inps o al proprio Caf). Il Bonus di un valore massimo di 500 euro è rivolto alle famiglie italiane composte da almeno tre persone. Per i nuclei familiari composti da due persone il Bonus vacanze scende a 300 euro, ma lo possono ottenere anche i single, in questo caso il valore è di 150 euro.
